segments.text: Honey never goes bad. Well, that's almost true. Sealed honey can last for thousands of years, but there's one way to ruin it.
Honey is mostly sugar and very little water. Germs need water to survive, so honey actually pulls the water right out of them.
In fact, honey is also acidic, about as sour as orange juice. Most bacteria simply can't live there.
Here's the wild part. Bees add an enzyme that slowly makes hydrogen peroxide. That's the same stuff used to clean cuts.
And if your honey turns hard and cloudy, it hasn't spoiled. It just crystallized. Warm the jar gently and it turns liquid again.
The one way to ruin it? Add water. Leave the lid open in a humid kitchen, and honey can start to ferment.
So keep the lid on, and your honey might outlive you.
